data.text: Looking at the current state, I have the cancer IHC scores computed (a18) and the normal IHC data in long format (a19–a22). I'll re-query the investigator in wide format (one row per gene, tissue as columns) with the reliability filter and highest-level rule, and in parallel add observation-count flags to the cancer table.

limitations: These are ordinal summaries computed from independent normal-tissue and cancer-tissue sample cohorts; they are not paired-patient measurements and do not reflect within-individual change.
The cancer weighted score is a continuous value derived from the proportion of tumour areas at each IHC level; it is not an ordinal category and should not be interpreted as a single IHC call.

Normal IHC levels reflect the highest ordinal level among Enhanced/Supported records for the specified cell type; a 'Not detected' level means no positive staining was observed in that cell type under those reliability criteria.
The heatmap leaves cells missing where a gene lacks both measurements for that tissue/cancer pair (e.g., 3 of the 12 colon-ranked genes lack lung normal IHC data).
Ties in the ranked list were broken by Ensembl ID ascending; the list is truncated to exactly 12 genes as requested.

limitations: Normal IHC is reduced to a single ordinal level per gene/tissue (the highest among Enhanced/Supported records); inter-observer variability and staining heterogeneity within the normal tissue are not captured.
Cancer IHC weighted scores pool all tumour samples of a given cancer type; tumour subtypes, grade and stage are not distinguished.
The ≥5-observation threshold for cancer IHC excludes genes with sparse tumour coverage; 1,580 of 5,573 genes have no cancer IHC row at all in the atlas.

The heatmap leaves cells missing where a gene lacks both measurements in a given pair (3 of 12 colon genes lack lung-pair data); these absences reflect missing atlas records, not confirmed absence of expression.
Colon consensus nTPM is a bulk-tissue RNA measure and may not reflect the protein level in the specific glandular cell type used for the normal IHC comparison.

limitations: The normal IHC level is a single ordinal call (highest level among Enhanced/Supported records) and does not capture the distribution of staining intensity across normal samples.

The cancer IHC weighted score aggregates counts across all tumour samples for a given cancer type; it is not a per-patient measurement and cannot be directly compared to the normal level on a patient-by-patient basis.
Genes with fewer than five cancer observations are excluded from the cancer score, which may bias the comparison toward well-studied genes.
The 'Not detected' normal level (score 0) may reflect true absence or a technical limitation of the IHC assay; it is treated as a valid zero in the scoring scheme.

Ties in the colon ranking at the 12th position were broken by Ensembl ID ascending; three genes (SLC3A2, NLGN1, SLC13A1, PTPRE, PDPN) share the same change value at the boundary, and the first twelve by Ensembl ID are reported.

items.text: Gene set: Predicted membrane proteins from HPA master table
Normal IHC table: highest ordinal level per gene/tissue (colon glandular, breast glandular, lung alveolar), Enhanced/Supported only
Cancer IHC table: weighted score per gene/cancer type (colorectal, breast, lung), >=5 observations
Per-pair summary: genes with both, median cancer-minus-normal, fraction increase >=1
Colon 12-gene detail: normal level/reliability, cancer counts, weighted score, change, colon consensus nTPM
Heatmap: 12 genes × 3 tissue/cancer pairs, unavailable cells missing
Interpretation: ordinal summaries of different samples, not paired-patient measurements
